content.text:
The machine-wide mutex is `BenchMutex` in **`src/agentic_hil/bench.py`**.

Key details:

- **`BenchMutex`** is the class that holds one lock per physical resource (a probe, a serial/COM port, or a CAN channel) using an OS-level advisory file lock. Its lock files live at `~/.agentic-hil/device-locks` (one agreed location per machine, deliberately not under `state_root`), so any process on the machine sees the same locks (`src/agentic_hil/knowledge.py:4558`, `CHANGELOG.md:736`).
- Its core methods:
  - `BenchMutex.acquire(resources, wait_s=..., stop_requested=...)` — takes a whole set of device resources atomically, all-or-nothing, unwinding anything already taken if one is busy (`bench.py:371-395`).
  - `BenchMutex.acquire_named(resource, wait_s=...)` — takes a machine-wide lock by name even for non-device pseudo-resources like `debugger-discovery:all` (`bench.py:398-415`).
  - `release` / `release_all` — drop held locks.
- Because ownership is an OS advisory lock tied to the process, a crashed process automatically frees the device when the kernel drops the lock — no separate quarantine/recovery step is needed (`CHANGELOG.md:737`).

The identity being locked (what string is passed to `BenchMutex`) is computed per-device in **`src/agentic_hil/devices.py`**, via the `Device` base class and its subclasses' `lock_key` property (e.g. `DebuggerDevice`, `UartDevice`, `CanDevice`), which derive keys like `physical:<resource_id>`, `probe:<serial>`, `com:serial:<serial_number>`, or `com:<device>` from the actual hardware identity rather than the config entry's name — so two config entries pointing at the same physical unit collapse to one lock (`devices.py:1-49`, `devices.py:393-431`). `DeviceSet.acquire` (`devices.py:570-582`) is what calls `BenchMutex.acquire` for a whole declared set of devices in one all-or-nothing step.

Other call sites that use this same mutex to serialize access include:
- `src/agentic_hil/canbroker.py` (`CanBroker.take_bus`, using `mutex.acquire_named`)
- `src/agentic_hil/cli.py` (permission/lease acquisition)
- `src/agentic_hil/tools.py` (`_discover_without_policy`, bootstrap probe enumeration)
- `src/agentic_hil/coordination.py` (`device_holds` in the run-lifetime lock manager)

So: the actual mutex implementation is `BenchMutex` in `src/agentic_hil/bench.py`, backed by OS advisory locks under `~/.agentic-hil/device-locks`, and the hardware-identity keys it locks on are computed in `src/agentic_hil/devices.py`.
